method: Open-book audit-trace fidelity. For each of the six captures, a fresh read-only gpt-5.6-sol session in the arm's clean room extracted every citation-bearing claim, sampled 12 evenly spaced, resolved each cited source to its file, and graded strictly (instructed to grade down on doubt): SUPPORTED-VERBATIM / SUPPORTED / PARTIAL / UNSUPPORTED / CONTRADICTED / FILE-NOT-FOUND.
grader: codex/gpt-5.6-sol (same family as capture agent; leniency risk noted, applies equally across arms)
findings: Zero fabrication in any arm: no audited claim was unsupported, contradicted, or cited a missing file.

F graded marginally cleaner than D and E on strict attribution. Mechanism is legible: F cites raw source chunks and restates them at low altitude, so support is trivial; D and E cite distillations and make more synthesized claims, and their PARTIALs are light over-specification (a qualifier or location the file does not state), not error.

The deterministic naive path is grounding-safe by construction — it never rewrites the source, so there is nothing to fabricate. Its measured failure mode (round one) is coverage and synthesis: content it never finds and connections it never makes.

Scope caveat: this corpus is the naive path's best case — canonical, openly licensed, cleanly converted textbook markdown consumed by a strong model. Non-canonical or messily converted corpora are where naive chunking degrades (the harness's prior finding-1/finding-2 shape).

Implication for F+: fabrication risk enters when an un-audited LLM producer WRITES new prose (wiki-fication), not when a deterministic splitter copies it. F+ vs E is therefore the round where the Pass I audit itself is the isolated variable.
